markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (61%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert
Input is flagged, InSitu stays in the 90% set, and MUSK disagrees [F6].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 61%, InSitu 38% | Leading class, not decisive |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive (90%) | Two classes not separable |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.77 / OOD 1.0, flagged | Image looks atypical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Top classes differ |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Invasive [F5] | Mostly supports Invasive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Scarce benign stroma/fat** (region 0) · ↑ invasive · Low score; concept model links scarcity to invasive [F3] · Validated
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 2, 6, 9) · ↑ invasive · High score, but only 3/20 spot-check regions acceptable [F4] · Unreliable
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 7) · ↓ invasive · Below typical; concept model counts it against invasive · Validated
- **Gland/tubule formation** (region 0) · ↑ invasive · Below-typical score; caption check inconsistent · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0: not shown faithful. Case leans on Unreliable necrosis and normal lobules.

## Could be wrong if
- Resampling degradation (simulated frozen section) distorts features and shifts probabilities.
- MUSK disagrees; InSitu (38%) stays plausible, and similar case BACH_0272 is InSitu.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 9, 3, 11**: highest heatmap contribution; look for stromal invasion versus in-situ ducts.
2. **Regions 2, 6, 9**: necrosis scored high but failed spot check; confirm it is real.
3. **Region 5**: lowest invasive risk (8%); check for duct-confined atypia.
